photo.caption: Bottom view of the Helios spacecraft. The three Zodiacal light photometers P15, P30, P90 show the black openings of their stray light baffles. The drift tube of the South (S) micrometeoroid sensor is seen next to the photometers.
photo.description: Bottom view of the Helios spacecraft showing the three Zodiacal light photometers P15, P30, and P90 as well as the South (S) micrometeoroid sensor.

photo.caption: P30, one of the three small photometers making up the zodiacal light instrument. In operation, the light enters from upper right through the black Carbon fibre stray light suppressing baffle.
photo.description: Helios P30 photometer. From left: photomultiplier with electronics, filter wheel, lens, baffle, and protective cover (removed before launch).

photo.caption: Display of the South and Ecliptic sensors and the common electronics box of the Helios Micrometeoroid Analyzer.

photo.caption: Repeatabiliy of Helios zodiacal light measurements from minimum (1975/1976) through maximum (1979/1980) of solar sunspot cycle 21. Red symbols indicate days with coronal mass ejections and enhanced plasma scattering. For comparison the brightness of Procyon was monitored.
photo.description: Repeatabiliy of Helios zodiacal light measuremens from minimum (1975/1976) through maximum (1979/1980) of solar sunspot cycle 21. Red symbols indicate days with coronal mass ejections and the enhanced scattering by high electron density. For confirmation of the instrumental stability the brightness of Procyon was monitored.
